clue.text: Posh girl's broadcasting is stylish

blocks.note: a deb (debutante) is an upper-class girl making her entry into society
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A society girl's radio presence is admired for its style.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a man who is suave, confident and elegantly dressed, a close synonym of stylish.

clue.text: Tracks unwashed smell to extremely dirty doormat

indicators.note: extremely points at the extremities of the next word, its two end letters only

blocks.note: to dog someone is to track or tail them
the standard two-letter abbreviation for the odour of an unwashed person
first and last letters of the word dirty

explanation.surface: Following the stink of someone unwashed leads to a filthy mat at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doormat' is not the mat in the scene but a person everyone walks over.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a put-upon person who does the menial chores and is treated with little respect.

clue.text: See 1
Demanded to be soundly massaged

indicators.note: soundly here means judged by sound, so the word is identified by how it is spoken

blocks.note: kneading is working muscles or dough with the hands, as a masseur does

explanation.surface: Someone insisted on getting a thorough massage.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent K means massaged and the answer are said identically.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needed is required or called for, as when a situation demanded action.

clue.text: Acting subeditor, in holding back article, is defiant

indicators.note: acting means performing a role, so these words take on a different form
holding means gripping something inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other
back tells us to read the following word from its end to its start

blocks.note: the two words taken as written to be rearranged
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A stand-in subeditor who refuses to print an article is behaving defiantly.
explanation.definitionFit: An insubordinate employee disobeys or defies those in authority, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Bosses don't have right to make mistakes

indicators.note: not having something means it is missing, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: gaffer is informal British for a boss or foreman
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Managers without the right of decision are bound to slip up.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is an embarrassing blunder, especially a social one, so gaffes are mistakes.

clue.text: Drink before dinner's appropriate, if Queen's first person to tuck in

indicators.note: tucking in means slipping something inside, so these pieces go within another

blocks.note: apt means fitting or appropriate
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
I is the first-person pronoun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pre-dinner drink is fine if Her Majesty is first to start eating.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to whet the appetite.

clue.text: Discovered iodine in a large quantity of make-up

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the chemical element goes within the quantity

blocks.note: found is the past tense of find, discovered
a ton is an informal big amount
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Someone found iodine in a big batch of cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Foundation is the cosmetic base applied to the face before other make-up.

clue.text: In case arm's hurt, boy's given dressing

indicators.note: hurt means damaged, so these letters are knocked out of their order
in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the jumbled letters

blocks.note: letters taken as written for rearranging
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy with an injured arm is bandaged up just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' plays on a wound dressing; it is the salad sort. Salad cream is a tangy British bottled dressing, like a thin mayonnaise.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad cream is a sauce poured over salad, which is what a dressing is in the kitchen.

clue.text: Leave daughters to oversee sons in finding wonderful women

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the following little word is read the other way round
the turned word is set around what follows it, as if it were put to work enclosing it

blocks.note: to go is to leave
D is the abbreviation for daughter, doubled for the plural
the second half of the word, after the turning signal, taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Parents leave the girls in charge of the boys while out looking for remarkable women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oversee' splits into OVER, the turning signal, and SEE, which wraps around the sons.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling admired, beautiful women goddesses is a common figurative compliment.

clue.text: Stay in bed late with injuries after doctor gives sedatives

blocks.note: to sleep in is to stay in bed later than usual
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
ills are harms or troubles

explanation.surface: A doctor prescribes something to calm a late sleeper who is hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeping pills are tablets taken to induce sleep, a kind of sedative.

clue.text: Even some casual jobs require qualifications

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the letters are found within the words that follow

blocks.note: surface padding that builds the picture of part-time work
letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Even part-time work demands formal qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb opening the sentence; it is the adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and equal are synonyms when describing scores or amounts that are level with each other.

clue.text: Idiotic complaint about care in Leeds cut short

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word before it reads backwards
in means placed inside, so one word sits within the city
something cut short loses its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: beef is slang for a grievance or complaint
the Yorkshire city, taken as written
to mind is to care or be concerned

explanation.surface: A daft grievance about the standard of care in Leeds was curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: MIND goes inside LEED, which is the city's name with its final S cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble-minded is a dated, unkind term for foolish or lacking intelligence, much as idiotic is.

clue.text: Direct look entirely disheartened oriental associate

indicators.note: losing its heart means the inside of the word is removed, leaving only its two ends

blocks.note: first and last letters of entirely
E is short for east, oriental meaning eastern
a contact is someone you associate with

explanation.surface: A downcast colleague from the East is given a straight look.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye contact is the act of looking directly into another person's eyes.

clue.text: Unquestioning confidence in sunscreen?

blocks.note: straight reading: faith given without asking questions
setter's reading: trust placed in a window shade that keeps out the sun

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: a screen against sunlight is a blind, so confidence in one is literally trust in a blind.
explanation.definitionFit: Blind trust is faith given without evidence or question, and the phrase also names a financial arrangement.

clue.text: The old record's painful noise

blocks.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
an LP is a long-playing vinyl record

explanation.surface: An ancient vinyl disc makes a dreadful racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A yelp is a sharp, short cry, typically of pain or surprise.

clue.text: Owner's in favour of pier renovation with Torquay losing wharf

indicators.note: renovation means rebuilding, so the letters of the structure are reworked
losing means giving something up, so part of the resort's name drops away

blocks.note: pro means for or in favour of
letters taken as written for rearranging
the Devon seaside town, taken as written
a quay is a wharf

explanation.surface: The owner supports rebuilding the pier, though Torquay will lose its wharf.
explanation.walkthrough: Torquay without QUAY leaves TOR; Torquay is a resort town on England's south-west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is the owner of a business or property.

clue.text: Engineer keen to get hold of advanced jet fuel

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or contrive, so these letters are rebuilt
getting hold of something means grasping it inside, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: letters taken as written for rearranging
rose is the past tense of rise, to advance or go up

explanation.surface: An eager engineer obtains advanced aviation fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a noun, the person; it is the verb that rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerosene, or paraffin, is the refined oil used as the main fuel in jet engines.

clue.text: One CV in ten gets rewritten, saving time and trouble

indicators.note: rewritten text is set down again in a new form, so these letters change order

blocks.note: all letters taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A recruiter says redrafting one application in ten is easier all round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something convenient fits easily into your plans, sparing effort and delay.

clue.text: Troubles brought about by drink in America

indicators.note: brought about is a sailing term for turning a ship round, so the word faces the other way

blocks.note: ados are fusses or troubles, as in much ado

explanation.surface: Problems caused by alcohol in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubles' looks like a verb with 'brought about' as its object; it is a noun. In the US, soda is the everyday word for a fizzy soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call any carbonated soft drink soda, where Britons might say pop or fizzy drink.

clue.text: Note villain's accent

blocks.note: B is a musical note
a rogue is a scoundrel or villain

explanation.surface: Pay attention to the bad guy's way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like an instruction to observe; it is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a strong regional accent, especially an Irish or Scottish one.

clue.text: Race to mountain by boat in area of outstanding natural beauty

blocks.note: a nation is a people or race
an alp is a high mountain
Noah's ark was a boat

explanation.surface: A dash to the summit by boat through glorious countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' reads as a contest; it means a people.
explanation.definitionFit: A national park is a protected area of scenic countryside, which the definition describes.

clue.text: Wound up crazy

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: bats is slang for mad, as in bats in the belfry

explanation.surface: Someone is wound up into a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound up' reads as a phrase meaning agitated, but the break falls between its two words: 'Wound' is a verb meaning to injure.
explanation.definitionFit: To stab someone is to wound them with a knife or other pointed weapon.

clue.text: In times gone by love's first noticed at church

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word that comes after it

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
opening letter of noticed
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Long ago, romance was first spotted in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some time in the past.

clue.text: Top grade's pretty clever

blocks.note: A is the highest exam grade
cute means attractive or pretty

explanation.surface: An A-grade result is fairly smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like an adverb meaning fairly; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute means sharp-witted and perceptive, so an acute mind is a clever one.

clue.text: Inform about losing weight?

blocks.note: first meaning: to give someone knowledge or understanding
second, playful meaning: to make lighter

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the whimsical second sense: making something lighter in weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlighten someone is to inform or educate them, and the word literally suggests making lighter.

clue.text: Look likely to fall for person who counts?

blocks.note: first meaning: to sway unsteadily on the point of toppling
second, playful meaning: one who tots up figures

explanation.walkthrough: To tot up is to add numbers, so the question mark admits an invented noun for someone doing so.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to walk or stand shakily, as if about to topple over.

clue.text: Form a group competent to contain rampant disorder

indicators.note: rampant means running wild, so the letters break out of their order
containing something means holding it inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: able means capable or competent
a mess is a state of disorder

explanation.surface: A capable team is formed to keep chaos in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather together into one place, forming a body of people.
